title: Week 39 Release Ops standup - campfire notes
body:
Context: informal capture from a 30m release-ops standup run Thursday morning (EMEA-friendly time). Focus was triage for the Week 39 train, preparing a minimal hotfix window Friday night US-west, and pre-canary signal tuning. These are notes + action items — not the final runbook but should be sufficient for engineers on-call and the release conductor to act on.

Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Date: 2025-09-29
Time: 09:00-09:30 PT
Attendees: Aisha, Diego, Lina, Owen, Priya, Jesse (+ SRE on-call: Marisol on standby)

Agenda (brief):
- Quick status across three release lanes (hosted api, dedicated, private)
- Hotfix appetite for regressed embedder latency spike
- Canary signal thresholds and rollout cadence for model v2.1.0
- Capacity headroom forecast for Friday night window
- Open asks / blockers

Quick status snapshots:
- Hosted API: train deploy for model v2.1.0 scheduled for 10/01 02:00 UTC. Smoke tests green in staging, perf bench shows median latency +3% vs v2.0.
- Dedicated: rolling upgrades paused on node pool A due to a reported driver mismatch (JIRA-4532). Patch validated on one node, but needs wider soak.
- Private: two customers on dedicated packages requested no changes this week; we respect freeze.

Hotfix backlog and decisions:
- Root problem: intermittent 95p token generation latency spikes traced to KV cache eviction storms when long-tail prompts arrive concurrently (see JIRA-4598).
- Decision: open a short hotfix window Friday 2025-10-03 01:00-02:30 UTC. Aim: deploy KV cache throttling patch (minor runtime change) + quick rollback capability.
- Risk: patch touches cache eviction heuristics; potential to increase tail latency for some multi-turn workloads. Mitigation: conservative default throttle, enable feature flag for canary groups only, monitor 95/99 percentiles closely.

Canary signal plan for v2.1.0:
- Canary cohort size: 2% of production traffic (routing flag via smart-router config).
- Metric set: 95p latency (text-gen), 99p latency (chat-stream), token error rate, CPU % on GPU host, KV cache miss rate.
- Triggers (automated):
  - Abort and automatic rollback if 99p latency increases >20% sustained for 5m
  - Pause if error rate >0.5% for 3m
  - Manual inspect if 95p rises 10% for 10m
- Observability owners: Lina (dashboards), Jesse (traces), Marisol (on-call ops).

Capacity planning for Friday window:
- Expected extra headroom request: +25% burst capacity for 90 minutes. Owen confirmed one spare pool in us-west with room for burst, but it requires pre-sizing to avoid cold-start overhead.
- Action: Owen to pre-scale 2x pods to warm state by 2025-10-03 00:30 UTC. (owner: Owen, due: 2025-10-03 00:30 UTC)

Action items (concise list):
- A1: Create the formal hotfix runbook (templates: rollback steps, owners, smoke tests, postmortem hooks). Owner: Aisha. Due: 2025-09-30 EOD. Linked: confluence draft above.
- A2: Land KV cache throttle patch behind a feature flag in canary branch; push to staging for soak. Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-09-30 12:00 PT. Jira: JIRA-4598.
- A3: Add 95/99p latency trace spans to the trace pipeline to identify offending request shapes quickly. Owner: Jesse. Due: 2025-09-30.
- A4: Pre-scale spare host pool in us-west; validate warm-start times and health checks. Owner: Owen. Due: 2025-10-03 00:30 UTC.
- A5: Update monitor playbook with new canary triggers and automatic rollback thresholds. Owner: Lina. Due: 2025-09-30.
- A6: Customer comms draft for two Private deployment customers confirming freeze window (informational only). Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-09-30.

Open questions and unresolved items:
- Q1: Do we need to adjust tokenization backoff for legacy models to reduce eviction pressure? (tbd by research/bench team)
- Q2: Are there any downstream SDKs that will surface transient 5xx behaviors during short throttling? Engineering to audit top-20 SDK clients. Owner: Diego, Jesse. Due: 2025-09-30.

Notes to self / post-standup thoughts (informal):
- Keep the hotfix window narrow and prefer feature-flag first approach. We lose more in customer trust with broad rollouts that increase tail latency.
- Consider adding a short-lived synthetic workload that mimics long-tail prompt bursts to exercise KV eviction patterns in staging prior to Friday. (Marisol volunteered to script this).

Risk register (short):
- R1: Mis-tuned throttle increases 95p for multi-turn chats — mitigation: canary + 2% cohort + manual gate.
- R2: Pre-scaling fails due to image pull or node pressure — mitigation: dry-run pre-scale tonight in a smaller pool.
- R3: On-call capacity stretched if we run both hosted canary + dedicated patch simultaneously — mitigation: stagger windows, keep SLO for pageouts at 1 per incident.

Wrap / next check-in:
- Next quick sync: Friday 2025-10-03 00:45 UTC (15m) — final go/no-go before patch push. Owner: Aisha to create calendar invite.
- Post-deploy: 1-hr rapid-observability window, then 24-hour watch for regression signals. Postmortem template will be pre-populated.

Linked tickets (for quick refs): JIRA-4532 (driver mismatch, dedicated pool A), JIRA-4598 (KV eviction/throttle patch), JIRA-4621 (canary alert tuning), JIRA-4633 (pre-scale validation failures).

If anything is missing, add to this doc and ping in #release-ops-bridge. These campfire notes are meant to be quick and a bit informal — I will convert the confirmed items into the runbook after Tuesday's engineering review.
